title: Send a task to someone who uses {name}, and get their answer back
description: Add a person once, side by side or with a link and six digits, then send them a task or what {name} made, sealed so that only they can open it.
answer: Add the person once in {settings} › {people}, side by side or with a link and six digits. Then, in {shareMenu}, choose {only} and send them a task or what {name} made: only they can open it, and their answer comes back into the same task.
steps.title: Add a person, then send
steps: Open {settings}, from the menu with your name (or “You”), at the foot of the task list, then {people}. Not there yet? Turn {people} on in {settings} › {capabilities}, or say in a task that you’d like to send something to someone.

Press {add} and type their name under {who}. Side by side, press {side}: they point their phone’s camera at the code, which works while it stays on your screen. Apart, press {apart} and send them the link the way you send them anything else: it works for a week.
On their side, {name} asks {from}: they type your name and press {accept}. Their screen then shows six digits, which they show you, or send back the way the link came.
Type those six digits on your screen and press {confirm}. You have three tries. If you closed {name} meanwhile, the digits are asked for under {invitations} when you open it again.
To send a task, press {shareMenu}, at the top of the task or in its ⋮ menu; under something {name} made, it is beside {copy}. Under {whoCan}, choose {only}, then the person.
Turn on {reading} to send the files {name} read too, add a note under {words} if you like, check what goes and its size, and press {send}. They have a week to open it.
good: What you send comes to them as a card above the conversation, on each of their devices, with {open} and {notNow}. Opened, it is a task of theirs that says it is from you: your requests stay yours, never theirs, and {name} asks them before sending anything out from it.

To answer, they choose “Send back to” and your name, in that task’s ⋮ menu: only what they added goes. Their answer comes to you as a card; {takeIn} adds it to the task you sent, after a line from them.

Only people added this way can be sent anything, and only they can open it: the six digits make sure the person is who you think. Each shows by the name you gave them, beside the name they give themselves; {rename} changes yours.
To remove someone, press {remove} beside their name in {people}. What they sent you stays yours.
The people you added follow you on your other devices. If you remove one of your devices, they get your new key by themselves; anyone marked “To meet again” is added again with the six digits.

At work, you may find your colleagues in {people} with {find}, then {keep}. For someone not there yet, press {inviteMail}: your own mail app opens with an email to them. Your organisation may also add people from its list alone; {add} then isn’t there.
Not in a child’s profile. To work on the same thing at once rather than send a copy, see {together}.
fixes: Type the six digits shown on their screen, not on yours. After three wrong tries it stops, to be safe: start again with {add}.
Up to 25 MB goes at once. Turn off {reading}, or send one part.
The invitation was already used, or ran out
A link adds one person, for a week. Press {add} for a new one.
They haven’t answered yet. Once they do, you can send them things.
